top_cited_works.title: A comparison between numerical calculations and experimental measurements of the structure of a counterflow diffusion flame burning diluted methane in diluted air
top_cited_works.abstract: Results of a theoretical and experimental study of the structure of a counterflow diffusion flame burning diluted methane in diluted air are reported. Concentration profiles of the stable species were measured using gas sampling techniques with quartz microprobes. The samples were analyzed with a gas chromatograph. Temperature profiles were measured using coated thermocouples. Numerical calculations of the structure of the flame were performed with an adaptive nonlinear boundary value method at conditions identical to those used in the experiment. The results are compared using both the physical coordinate and the mixture fraction as the independent variable. Excellent agreement is obtained for concentration profiles of CH4, O2, N2, CO2 and H2O and for the peak value of the temperature. The complete temperature profile and the H2 and CO profiles are not in as good agreement and the differences are attributed to the neglect of C2 chemistry in the numerical calculations.

3D Cell Printing and Manipulation with Magnetic Bioinks
recent_works.abstract: Three-dimensional (3D) cell culture models more faithfully reproduce native tissue organization and function than conventional two-dimensional systems, yet many existing bioprinting methods depend on scaffolds, complex instrumentation, or limited control over cell positioning. This review examines magnetic bioinks as a versatile platform for contactless 3D cell manipulation and biofabrication. It first outlines the fundamentals of magnetophoresis and defines magnetic bioinks as combinations of magnetic agents, including magnetic nanoparticles or paramagnetic salts, with biological components such as cells, proteins, or fluids. The review then compares label-based strategies, in which cells are magnetized and guided by positive magnetophoresis, with label-free approaches that exploit magnetic susceptibility differences to position diamagnetic cells through negative magnetophoresis. Across these methods, magnetic bioinks have enabled single-cell sorting, spatial patterning, spheroid and co-culture assembly, multilayer tissue formation, and hydrogel-integrated printing. recent_works.title: Assessing the Safety and Efficacy of Self-Expanding Metallic Y Stents in a Community Medicine Setting
recent_works.venue: American Journal of Respiratory and Critical Care Medicine
recent_works.abstract: Abstract Background: Y stents are a specialized tool specifically designed for tracheobronchial anatomy that is most often used in the setting of central airway obstruction and fistulae. Historically, silicone Y stents have been used for the purpose of maintaining structure of the central airways, but over the past few years self-expanding metallic (SEM) Y stents have emerged as potential alternative. There is limited data on its efficacy in achieving similar results as silicone Y stents. Objective: To evaluate the outcomes of the treatment of benign and malignant central airway obstruction and fistulae in a community center after appropriate tracheobronchial re-cannulation with self-expanding metallic Y stent. Methods: A retrospective analysis of 14 patients over the span of 22 months from August 2022 to June 2024 who underwent SEM Y stent placement was conducted. Data collected included patient demographics, indication for stent placement, procedural details, complications, and duration of stent placement prior to removal or discharge to hospice. recent_works.title: Modifying metal ion ratios in nickel-aluminum layered double hydroxide/reduced graphene oxide composites for selective electrochemical detection of antibiotics
recent_works.abstract: • A low-temperature hydrothermal method is optimized for synthesizing nickel-aluminium layered hydroxide and its graphene composite. • A novel metal-ion ratio concept is hypothesized for detecting antibiotics from their cocktail, and it is demonstrated using nickel-aluminium layered double hydroxides (NiAl-LDH) as a tunable active material. • Promising sensor properties are shown by using graphene oxide composite with good selectivity. Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is a global threat that occurs as microorganisms evolve to resist antibiotic (ATB) overuse. To monitor this overuse, inexpensive, affordable, and adaptable sensors are required. While electrochemical sensors are promising, they cannot often distinguish between overlapping electrochemical interactions from multiple ATBs, resulting in poor analyte selectivity. To overcome this challenge, we design electrocatalysts consisting of nickel aluminum layered double hydroxides (NiAl-LDH) and their composites by altering the metal ion ratio to adjust the surface properties and selectivity of sensors.
